summary: This concise manuscript constructs TENSOR-SPECTRUM-CONN-CERT-1.0, a zero-float, exact-Z/Q verification and constructive Lean 4.36.0 certificate suite motivated by Vrana and Zuiddam's path-connectedness theorem for Strassen's asymptotic spectrum. Across 20 Lean theorems (T01-T20) and 16 SHA-256-indexed rational certificates (C01-C16), it certifies: (i) exact 3-mode flattening ranks and Kronecker/direct-sum laws across matrix multiplication tensors, W3, CW2, and CW3; (ii) root-free integer-power interval bounds, strict simplex-edge monotonicity, and volume-square identities for <a,b,c>; (iii) an 8-entry Z[epsilon] border-rank-2 identity for W3 with the exact gap 27/4 < 8 and 27^k < 32^k amplification; and (iv) exact graph capacity sandwiches for C5 (size-5 independent set in C_5^{strong 2}) and C7 (Chebyshev root bracket on 8t^3-4t^2-4t+1 giving theta(C7) in (63/19, 637/191)). All equations, rational identities, plots, and Table 1 entries in the PDF are exact, and Section 5 transparently delineates mechanized claims from imported theorems. Aside from minor expositional nuances (such as Figure 1's edge legend direction and general-tensor naming of zeta_theta), this is solid verified work.
strengths: Every rational identity, polynomial evaluation, flattening rank, and inequality in Theorems 2.1, 3.1, and 4.1, Figures 1-3, and Table 1 is exact and root-free, avoiding floating-point approximation.

Section 5 states a crisp, transparent verification boundary explicitly separating the 20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems and 16 rational certificates from imported literature results (Vrana-Zuiddam, Strassen, Lovasz).

The C7 Lovasz-theta sandwich is cleanly reduced to exact rational polynomial evaluations p(9/10)=-1/125 and p(91/100)=9521/125000 plus derivative positivity p'(t)>0 on t>=9/10, giving (63/19, 637/191).
The W3 border-rank-2 witness over Z[epsilon] and cleared-denominator separation 27^k < 32^k provide an elementary, fully explicit algebraic certification of the non-degenerate spectral gap.
weaknesses: The newly mechanized Lean theorems (T01-T20) formalize elementary integer inequalities, polynomial brackets, and finite rank or independent-set checks, while all deep theorems (path-connectedness, duality, theta formula) remain unproved external imports.

Section 2 calls zeta_theta the Strassen geometric interpolation functional and Figure 1 labels it Strassen Support Functional; while this agrees with F_theta on <a,b,c>, for general tensors the geometric mean of flattening ranks is not direct-sum additive and not in Delta(T_3).
Figure 1 (left) exhibits a minor legend direction slip: the orange curve 10^(1-t) 15^t runs from e3 (10) at t=0 to e2 (15) at t=1, whereas the legend labels it Edge e2 -> e3.

Theorem 3.1(2) relies on Strassen's 1991 upper bound on asymptotic subrank of W3 being <= 2^(h(1/3)) to interpret 27/4 < 8 as a spectral interval width for W3, without explicitly citing Strassen (1991) in the 5-item bibliography.
strong_novelty_candidates: Root-free, cleared-denominator Lean 4.36.0 and exact-Q certification suite (TENSOR-SPECTRUM-CONN-CERT-1.0) bridging Vrana-Zuiddam spectral interpolation examples with zero-axiom constructive proofs.

Exact rational Chebyshev bracket on p(t)=8t^3-4t^2-4t+1 with certified derivative positivity on [9/10, infinity) isolating Lovasz theta(C7) strictly inside (63/19, 637/191) without floating-point arithmetic.
